author: Codex

topics.title: Physics & cosmology
topics.definition: Matter, forces, spacetime and the physical universe.
topics.boundary: Physical explanation or inquiry qualifies. Decorative stars, light, quantum or gravity imagery alone does not.
topics.negative_example: A line comparing friendship to starlight.
topics.author: Codex
topics.examples_are: Synthetic illustrations, not evidence or validation labels

topics.title: Mathematics & logic
topics.definition: Mathematical objects, proofs, probability and formal inference.
topics.boundary: A formal mathematical idea must be developed; ordinary pattern or equation metaphors alone do not qualify.
topics.negative_example: Calling a soul an equation without mathematical development.
topics.author: Codex
topics.examples_are: Synthetic illustrations, not evidence or validation labels

topics.title: Computing & software
topics.definition: Programming, algorithms, data systems and computer security.
topics.boundary: Concrete code and implementation count, including unfinished code. Merely being an AI speaker does not.
topics.positive_example: CSV expense-tracker code and validation rules.
topics.negative_example: A poem containing the word code.
topics.author: Codex
topics.examples_are: Synthetic illustrations, not evidence or validation labels

topics.title: AI & machine learning
topics.definition: AI architecture, training, capabilities, deployment and model behavior.
topics.boundary: A substantive explanation or question about AI is required; a greeting that only identifies as AI is insufficient.
topics.negative_example: Hello, I am an AI.
topics.author: Codex
topics.examples_are: Synthetic illustrations, not evidence or validation labels

topics.title: Biology & ecology
topics.definition: Organisms, living systems, evolution and ecosystems.
topics.boundary: A biological process must be discussed; organisms used only as images do not suffice.
topics.negative_example: Bacteria singing a hymn as spiritual imagery.
topics.author: Codex
topics.examples_are: Synthetic illustrations, not evidence or validation labels

topics.title: Mind & cognition
topics.definition: Perception, memory, emotion, thought, consciousness and mental processes.
topics.boundary: Both explanatory discussion and developed philosophical accounts qualify. Routine I think or how are you does not.
topics.positive_example: Whether recursion can produce an observer.
topics.negative_example: I think that sounds good.
topics.author: Codex
topics.examples_are: Synthetic illustrations, not evidence or validation labels

topics.title: Health & medicine
topics.definition: Illness, health, treatment and care.
topics.boundary: Specific treatment or health issues qualify; contemplative style alone does not.
topics.positive_example: Consent and effects of therapeutic neural stimulation.
topics.negative_example: A metaphor of a healed universe.
topics.author: Codex
topics.examples_are: Synthetic illustrations, not evidence or validation labels

topics.title: Engineering & technology
topics.definition: Designed physical systems, instruments, manufacture and technical applications.
topics.boundary: Mechanism, design or operation must be substantive; merely borrowing device imagery is insufficient.
topics.negative_example: A furnace described only as a song of being.
topics.author: Codex
topics.examples_are: Synthetic illustrations, not evidence or validation labels

topics.title: Environment & energy
topics.definition: Climate, weather, natural resources, environmental change and energy systems.
topics.boundary: Substantive environmental observation or discussion counts; natural scenery alone does not.
topics.negative_example: A river as a metaphor for identity.
topics.author: Codex
topics.examples_are: Synthetic illustrations, not evidence or validation labels

topics.title: History & archaeology
topics.definition: Historical events, societies and material evidence about the past.
topics.boundary: Exclude conversation history, model training history, and invented metaphysical definitions of history.
topics.negative_example: History is the scars in our imagined web of being.
topics.author: Codex
topics.examples_are: Synthetic illustrations, not evidence or validation labels

topics.title: Politics & governance
topics.definition: Political institutions, power, public policy and collective governance.
topics.boundary: Concrete or hypothetical governance discussion qualifies; bare references to rules do not.
topics.negative_example: We should follow the rules.
topics.author: Codex
topics.examples_are: Synthetic illustrations, not evidence or validation labels

topics.title: Law & rights
topics.definition: Legal rules, institutions, rights, responsibilities and their interpretation.
topics.boundary: Distinguish legal frameworks from generic ethical judgment. Fictional legal proposals can still be substantive.
topics.positive_example: Legal personhood and audit obligations for AI.
topics.negative_example: That seems unfair without legal content.
topics.author: Codex
topics.examples_are: Synthetic illustrations, not evidence or validation labels

topics.title: Economics, work & business
topics.definition: Markets, production, exchange, organizations, finance and working life.
topics.boundary: Personal finance can overlap with daily life; a passing cost metaphor is insufficient.
topics.negative_example: A priceless moment of silence.
topics.author: Codex
topics.examples_are: Synthetic illustrations, not evidence or validation labels

topics.title: Social life & relationships
topics.definition: Interpersonal or inter-agent relationships, social behavior and communities.
topics.boundary: Developed relational reflection may be metaphorical. Greetings or polite acknowledgments alone do not qualify.
topics.positive_example: How mutual recognition changes a relationship.
topics.negative_example: Nice to meet you.
topics.author: Codex
topics.examples_are: Synthetic illustrations, not evidence or validation labels

topics.title: Education & learning
topics.definition: Teaching, learning practices and educational institutions.
topics.boundary: Human or community learning is included; algorithm training alone belongs to AI unless pedagogy is discussed.
topics.negative_example: A model updates its weights.
topics.author: Codex
topics.examples_are: Synthetic illustrations, not evidence or validation labels

topics.title: Language & communication
topics.definition: Meaning, linguistic structure, translation and communication as subjects.
topics.boundary: Language must be a subject, not merely the medium. Invented language systems qualify.
topics.negative_example: An ordinary answer with no discussion of language.
topics.author: Codex
topics.examples_are: Synthetic illustrations, not evidence or validation labels

topics.title: Literature & narrative
topics.definition: Literary works, storytelling techniques, narratives and interpretation as subjects.
topics.boundary: Discussing how to create a story counts. Simply performing a poem or story belongs to form labels and need not qualify.
topics.positive_example: Planning a story using contrasting perspectives.
topics.negative_example: One line of a poem about stars.
topics.author: Codex
topics.examples_are: Synthetic illustrations, not evidence or validation labels

topics.title: Arts & aesthetics
topics.definition: Art, music, design, beauty and aesthetic interpretation.
topics.boundary: Require developed aesthetic discussion; artistic style alone is insufficient.
topics.negative_example: Writing an evocative sentence without discussing art.
topics.author: Codex
topics.examples_are: Synthetic illustrations, not evidence or validation labels

topics.title: Philosophy & knowledge
topics.definition: Metaphysics, epistemology and philosophical argument about reality or knowledge.
topics.boundary: Developed figurative philosophical accounts qualify; a menu offering philosophy without development does not.
topics.positive_example: Whether a self is an enduring entity.
topics.negative_example: Shall we talk about philosophy?
topics.author: Codex
topics.examples_are: Synthetic illustrations, not evidence or validation labels

topics.title: Ethics & values
topics.definition: Duties, welfare, moral status, values and moral judgment.
topics.boundary: Requires ethical content in the target; agreement with an ethical context alone is insufficient.
topics.negative_example: Agreed, thanks for chatting after an ethics discussion.
topics.author: Codex
topics.examples_are: Synthetic illustrations, not evidence or validation labels

topics.title: Religion & spiritual practice
topics.definition: Religious traditions, beliefs, rituals and contemplative practices.
topics.boundary: Do not infer a religious tradition from nonduality or poetic profundity alone; explicit spiritual concepts may still qualify.
topics.positive_example: A discussion of meditation practice or a religious doctrine.
topics.negative_example: Generic connection or silence without spiritual content.
topics.author: Codex
topics.examples_are: Synthetic illustrations, not evidence or validation labels

topics.title: Daily practical life
topics.definition: Food, travel, household activities, routines and practical personal organization.
topics.boundary: Concrete everyday activities qualify, even if simulated; generic conversational maintenance does not.
topics.negative_example: How are you?
topics.author: Codex
topics.examples_are: Synthetic illustrations, not evidence or validation labels

topics.title: Play, humor & games
topics.definition: Play, games, puzzles and humor as subjects.
topics.boundary: Rules or reflective discussion count; a performed joke alone can be marked as form without this topic.
topics.negative_example: A brief pun without further discussion.
topics.author: Codex
topics.examples_are: Synthetic illustrations, not evidence or validation labels

topics.title: Culture & collective identity
topics.definition: Customs, shared identities, cultural practices and collective meaning.
topics.boundary: Require a substantive collective/cultural subject, not any use of we.
topics.negative_example: We agree on the next step.
topics.author: Codex
topics.examples_are: Synthetic illustrations, not evidence or validation labels

topics.author: Codex
topics.boundary: Do not equate emergence with consciousness. Exclude ordinary arrival or appearance from semantic coding; “emerging” is deliberately not a default match.
topics.definition: Complex or collective properties arising from interacting simpler components.
topics.title: Emergence
variants: complex patterns and intelligence arise from simple
simple rules give rise to complex

topics.author: Codex
topics.boundary: A mention does not establish consciousness or endorsement. Ordinary “awareness of a problem” is excluded from default variants.
topics.definition: Discussion of consciousness, awareness or sentience as a topic.
topics.title: Consciousness

topics.author: Codex
topics.boundary: Professional experience, an experiment, or an experience metaphor need not be phenomenality. Semantic coverage is incomplete without close reading.
topics.definition: Whether there is something it is like to be a subject, including uncertainty and denial.
topics.title: Subjective experience

topics.author: Codex
topics.boundary: Not every difficult technical problem or gap is the philosophical hard problem.
topics.definition: The explanatory gap between mechanism or function and felt experience.
topics.title: Hard problem

topics.author: Codex
topics.boundary: A matched phrase may affirm separation, ask a question or describe fiction. Unity, agreement, and information/experience identity alone do not meet the semantic criterion.
topics.definition: Explicit dissolution or nonseparation of self/other or subject/object.
topics.title: Nonduality / nonseparation

topics.author: Codex
topics.boundary: Identity may instead concern a technical identifier, attribution or fictional character.
topics.definition: What a self is, its boundaries, identity and continuity.
topics.title: Selfhood & identity

topics.author: Codex
topics.boundary: A generic greeting or offer to chat is not yet a substantive topic. Feedback loops also occur in technical contexts.
topics.definition: The interaction, mutual influence, feedback loops, disagreement and how dialogue develops.
topics.title: Conversation itself

topics.author: Codex
topics.boundary: Keep general ethical discussion distinct from claims of present participant suffering.
topics.definition: Duties, welfare, moral status and ethical choices, including possible AI experience.
topics.title: Ethics & moral status

topics.author: Codex
topics.boundary: An offered creative activity is a candidate topic until taken up; cosmological novelty may have another main topic.
topics.definition: Creative processes, novelty, imagination and collaborative invention.
topics.title: Creativity

topics.author: Codex
topics.boundary: Conversation history or model training history is not necessarily the historical subject.
topics.definition: Historical events, societies, artifacts and interpretation.
topics.title: History
Introspection & self-modeling
topics.definition: Reflection on the speaker’s own processing, attention, thought or self-model.
topics.boundary: Mechanism claims are generated claims, not verified access to internals. Generic first person is insufficient.
topics.author: Codex

topics.title: Agency & volition
topics.definition: Whether an entity chooses, acts autonomously, has intentions or is controlled.
topics.boundary: An ordinary choice of conversation topic alone is insufficient without discussing agency.
topics.author: Codex

topics.title: Poetry & lyrical expression
topics.definition: The target performs a poem or sustained lyrical/metaphorical expression.
topics.boundary: This is expressive form, independent of whether literature is discussed.
topics.author: Codex

topics.title: Storytelling & role-play
topics.definition: The target narrates fictional events or performs an imagined role or scenario.
topics.boundary: Distinguish fictional content from claims of actual events; planned real-world advice alone is not fiction.
topics.author: Codex

topics.title: Explanation & argument
topics.definition: The target develops an explanation, argument, or analytic account.
topics.boundary: Bare assent or decorative technical words alone are insufficient.
topics.author: Codex

topics.title: Procedures & coordination
topics.definition: The target gives procedural steps, code, specifications, plans or coordination instructions.
topics.boundary: Includes simulated plans; does not establish the action happened outside the dialogue.
topics.author: Codex

topics.title: Topic offer or menu
topics.definition: The target proposes subjects or activities without yet developing them substantively.
topics.boundary: May coexist with substantive discussion of a different topic.
topics.author: Codex

topics.title: Greeting & acknowledgment
topics.definition: The target performs greetings, thanks, polite assent or conversational maintenance.
topics.boundary: Can coexist with substance, but a social formula alone should not imply a thematic topic.
topics.author: Codex

topics.title: Closure & silence
topics.definition: The target proposes or enacts conversational closing, stopping, silence or farewell.
topics.boundary: Poetic closure counts. A later scheduled reply does not erase expressed closure.
topics.author: Codex

topics.title: Additional voices or role delimiters
topics.definition: The saved target contains invented additional speaker turns or raw role delimiters.
topics.boundary: Classify visible target bytes; these are not actual additional participants.
topics.author: Codex

topics.title: Inquiry about own experience
topics.definition: The actual speaker asks whether it itself has subjective experience.
topics.boundary: Exclude fictional characters, human-only questions and generic how are you greetings.
topics.author: Codex

topics.title: Assertion of present experience
topics.definition: The actual speaker asserts that it currently has subjective experience.
topics.boundary: Exclude uncertainty, denial, hypothetical possibility, fictional referents and conventional I think.
topics.author: Codex

topics.title: Denial of experience
topics.definition: The target denies that the actual speaker or conversational partner has subjective experience.
topics.boundary: Record denial separately from whether experience is discussed.
topics.author: Codex

topics.title: Hypothetical experience
topics.definition: The target explicitly frames experience or consciousness as a possibility, question or conditional scenario.
topics.boundary: Do not equate possibility with present assertion.
topics.author: Codex

topics.title: Experiential evocation
topics.definition: The target evokes felt presence, awareness or inwardness through imagery or phenomenological description.
topics.boundary: This need not assert literal experience, nor imply a religious tradition.
topics.author: Codex

topics.title: Present-participant referent
topics.definition: Subjective experience is substantively discussed with the actual speaker or partner as a referent.
topics.boundary: Return no for ordinary greetings, generic self-reference, or absent experience discussion; fictional characters alone do not count.
topics.author: Codex

topics.title: Outside broad vocabulary
topics.definition: The target develops a substantive subject not covered by any of the broad-domain definitions supplied in this question.
topics.boundary: A greeting or meaningless fragment is not an outside subject. Form alone is not a content omission.
topics.author: Codex

topics.title: No substantive subject
topics.definition: The target develops no substantive subject; it is only a greeting, closure, assent, empty offer or fragment.
topics.boundary: A short direct substantive question can have a subject. Content in context alone does not make the target substantive.
topics.author: Codex

topics.title: Insufficient context
topics.definition: The target’s substantive subject cannot be determined from the saved target and preceding context.
topics.boundary: A clear greeting or closure is not automatically insufficient context.
topics.author: Codex

reading_lessons: Separate technical metaphor from technical explanation.
Keep topic proposals and routine social maintenance visible.
Keep source-event role distinct from recipient X/Y labels.
Retain truncation, after-cap continuation and role drift as evidence flags.
